a1-1-alphabet.lastLine: Das sind Umlaute . Wir üben zusammen !
a1-1-alphabet.intro: Frau Weber's very first German lesson in Berlin. She welcomes new student Rohan — and the first thing he learns is how to spell his own name, letter by letter, and where those two little dots come from.

a1-10-artikel.lastLine: Danke , Julia ! Jetzt verstehe ich das !
a1-10-artikel.intro: Kai points around the classroom and Julia names each object — but every noun comes with a colour: der, die or das. A quick trick turns the hardest habit in German into a game.

a1-11-negation.intro: Lunchtime talk. Ben has no time, Anna has no more money, and the two learn the two ways to say no in German — kein for things, nicht for everything else.

a1-12-akkusativ.lastLine: Schön ! Wir haben alles . Wir sind gut !
a1-12-akkusativ.intro: Tom and Lisa go shopping after class. Tom is looking for a few things — and every object he wants becomes a direct object in the accusative.

a1-13-adjektive.lastLine: st sehr gut ! Berlin ist jetzt dein Zuhause .
a1-13-adjektive.intro: Marie asks Leon to describe his city and his friends. With sein and an adjective, Leon paints a picture of his new life in Berlin.

a1-14-essen.lastLine: gern ! Ich trinke immer Tee . Danke , Hanna !
a1-14-essen.intro: Hanna is working at a café in Berlin when Simon comes in for breakfast — and the food words arrive before any rule does.

a1-15-cafe.intro: After class, Ida drops into a café in Kreuzberg. The waiter takes her order, the prices come up, and she settles the bill — every café phrase you need, in one real scene.

a1-16-hobbies.intro: It is Friday after class. Elias asks Sara about the weekend, and their hobbies come out — Sara’s tennis, Elias’s photography, and one firm preference for the sofa.

a1-17-goethe2.lastLine: st richtig . Willkommen an der Sprachschule !
a1-17-goethe2.intro: Jan signs up for the Goethe exam. Frau Roth helps him fill out the registration form line by line — family name, address, postcode, email — so every piece of personal info from Chapters 1–16 gets one more workout.

a1-18-irregular.lastLine: r ! Es gibt immer Kuchen . Bis zwölf , Nora !
a1-18-irregular.intro: A normal morning at the Uni. Nora and Timo sort out how they get there, who's too tired, who sees the library, and whether there's cake in the Mensa — and almost every verb in the scene is an irregular one changing its stem.

a1-19-satzposition.intro: Pia asks Lukas about his daily routine, and Lukas chimes in with his (not very disciplined) version. As they compare mornings, noons and nights, the verb keeps landing in the same place — position 2 — no matter what word starts the sentence.

a1-2-vokale.lastLine: Kurz ! Das a ist kurz . Sehr gut , Jonas !
a1-2-vokale.intro: Second lesson, pure sound. Frau Bauer coaches Jonas through the five German vowels and the umlauts that Hindi does not have — and Jonas finds his inner German.

a1-20-modalverben1.intro: A party is coming. Jule wants to plan it, Finn definitely wants to come, and Finn must finish his homework first. As they sort out who can do what, every sentence shows the same shape — modal in position 2, main verb at the very end.

a1-21-uhrzeit.lastLine: . Dann kommen wir um halb acht . Bis morgen !
a1-21-uhrzeit.intro: After the party plan, the group needs a time. Mara checks the calendar — her class runs until the afternoon — while Jonas, predictably, wants the latest possible start. Watch how every appointment locks onto the clock with um, am and von…bis.

a1-22-berufe.lastLine: Schön ! Dann hast du einen guten Job .
a1-22-berufe.intro: Career day comes up in the canteen. Lea wants to be a doctor, Erik has just landed an engineering job, and between the two of them the two job patterns keep resurfacing: Ich bin … and Ich arbeite als …
a1-22-berufe.scene: In der Mensa — über Berufe, Berlin

a1-23-familie.lastLine: wohnen hier in Berlin . Das ist sehr schön .
a1-23-familie.intro: Ines brings a family photo to the canteen. As she and Nils pass it around, every "this is my…/her…/his…" puts a possessive article to work — and Ines, of course, has a photo of someone unexpected.

a1-24-datum.lastLine: erfekt ! Gut : die Feier ist am zweiten Mai .
a1-24-datum.intro: Katja's birthday is coming. Katja and Tobias plan a surprise party around the calendar — fixing the date, counting the guests, and sorting out gifts — so ordinal numbers and months come up in every line.

a1-25-trennbar.lastLine: Ach so ! Dann bis halb zwölf !
a1-25-trennbar.intro: Saturday morning. Svenja calls Malte to plan the day — getting up, shopping, picking him up — and almost every plan is a separable verb whose prefix lands, with a little click, at the end of the sentence.

a1-26-goethe3.lastLine: Perfekt ! Dann bis morgen um vier !
a1-26-goethe3.intro: The study group agreed to meet at four to prepare for the checkpoint. It's ten past — and Britta is missing again. When she finally arrives, the lesson becomes a real one: how to apologise, accept an apology, and arrange the next appointment, German-style.

a1-27-praeteritum.lastLine: Oh ! Dann war mein Tag zu Hause besser !
a1-27-praeteritum.intro: Monday morning. Doris missed the weekend get-together, so Kai fills her in on what happened — where everyone was, who had cake, and why the weekend was, as usual, eventful. Every sentence lands in the past with war and hatte.

a1-28-perfekt.lastLine: Ja ! Heute trinken wir zusammen Kaffee !
a1-28-perfekt.intro: Tuesday. Jens asks Vera the most natural question in the world — what did you do yesterday? He travelled and visited his brother; she worked and had only coffee. Every answer arrives in the Perfekt: a helper verb up front, a participle at the end.
a1-28-perfekt.scene: Im Kurs — "Was hast du gemacht?", Berlin

a1-29-perfekt-haben.lastLine: ung zusammen gemacht . Jetzt haben wir frei !
a1-29-perfekt-haben.intro: The exam is over. In the café, Miriam and Robert compare how they prepared — who studied for two weeks, who read every question, who drank too much coffee. Every line is a haben-Perfekt: habe gelernt, hat gelesen, haben getrunken.
a1-29-perfekt-haben.scene: Nach der Prüfung — im Café, Berlin

a1-3-zahlen.intro: Third lesson, and two classmates finally get properly acquainted — names, ages, and the all-important phone-number swap. Emma reels off her digits; Tim needs them a little slower.

a1-30-perfekt-sein.lastLine: Nur drei Tage . Dann fahre ich zurück .
a1-30-perfekt-sein.intro: Ole is back from a short trip and Steffi wants every detail — where he flew, when he arrived, how long he stayed. His whole story runs on sein-Perfekt: bin geflogen, ist angekommen, sind geblieben.
a1-30-perfekt-sein.scene: Nach der Reise — im Kurs, Berlin

a1-31-partizip-praefix.lastLine: Noch nicht . Aber ich mache das jetzt !
a1-31-partizip-praefix.intro: A lot happened yesterday. Wanda got a package, her brother took her book before she could read it, and Timo — forgot the whole thing. As they catch up, every verb has a prefix: some keep ge- in the middle, some drop it completely.
a1-31-partizip-praefix.scene: Vor dem Kurs — was gestern passiert ist, Berlin

a1-32-akkusativpronomen.lastLine: Gern ! Aber nimm ihn heute mit !
a1-32-akkusativpronomen.intro: The class is planning a little party. Who is bringing the cake, who is calling Ronja, who has the music? As the group sorts out the jobs, every answer swaps the noun for a pronoun — ihn, sie, es, uns — so nobody has to repeat themselves.

a1-33-saetze-verbinden.intro: Weekend plans are up in the air. Carla wants to go out, but Jonas has a reason to stay in — work — and, as ever, an excuse ready. As they argue it out, every sentence gets glued to the next with und, aber, denn, deshalb and weil.

a1-34-schreiben.lastLine: Ja , ich sende sie gleich an alle .
a1-34-schreiben.intro: Petra is throwing a birthday party and needs two messages: a casual WhatsApp to the gang and a formal email to invite Petra. As the group helps her write both, the difference between "Hi, kommst du?" and "Sehr geehrte Petra" comes alive.
a1-34-schreiben.scene: Eine Einladung schreiben — im Kurs, Berlin

a1-35-goethe4.lastLine: toll . Nächstes Jahr komme ich noch einmal .
a1-35-goethe4.intro: Runa is back from a trip and has written a little holiday report. As she reads it out and the group reacts, almost every structure from Phase 4 surfaces — the Perfekt, war and hatte, pronouns, weil and deshalb — a perfect warm-up before the checkpoint.
a1-35-goethe4.scene: Vor dem Checkpoint — Runas Reisebericht, Berlin

a1-36-dativ.intro: It's gift time before the holidays. Alina gives the teacher flowers, helps a classmate, and — of course — saves herself the last piece of cake. Every "to whom?" puts the dative to work — dem, der, den — the case of the receiver.
a1-36-dativ.scene: Geschenke vor den Ferien — im Kurs, Berlin

a1-37-praep-dativ.lastLine: Gute Idee ! Dann fahren wir zusammen .
a1-37-praep-dativ.intro: The group is planning a weekend trip to Munich. Who travels how, who they’re staying with, how long they’ve studied German — every answer rides on a dative preposition: mit dem Zug, bei der Tante, seit einem Jahr.

a1-38-wechselpraep.lastLine: Danke ! Die Wohnung sieht bald schön aus .
a1-38-wechselpraep.intro: Franzi has a new flat and the gang is helping her move in. As they decide where the sofa, the lamp and the pictures go, the two-way prepositions come alive: putting things somewhere is accusative (Wohin?), and where they already sit is dative (Wo?).

a1-39-ortsangaben.intro: Meike is lost on the way to a new café and calls Timo for directions. As he walks her there — left, right, straight on, past the pharmacy — the location words and the everyday contractions (zum, zur, am, ins) do all the work.
a1-39-ortsangaben.scene: Auf dem Weg — eine Wegbeschreibung, Berlin

a1-4-hallo.lastLine: Auf Wiedersehen , Frau Klein ! Bis bald !
a1-4-hallo.intro: David arrives at his Berlin language school and meets the receptionist, Frau Klein. A first, formal conversation — Sie, Herr and Frau — and he learns exactly when Germans switch to the friendly du.

a1-40-verben-dativ.intro: Nele needs an outfit for a party and drags the gang to a clothes shop. As they judge every jacket, dress and pair of shoes, the dative verbs do the talking: Das gefällt mir, das passt dir, der Mantel steht dir — and Nele, of course, helps no one.
a1-40-verben-dativ.scene: Im Kleidergeschäft — ein Outfit für die Party, Berlin

a1-41-dativpronomen.intro: Five minutes before class and nobody has what they need. Frau Sommer is the one asking now — for the soup, for water, for a favour — and the waiter obliges every time: Ich bringe es Ihnen, ich bringe Ihnen das Wasser sofort. Every favour swaps a name for a dative pronoun.
a1-41-dativpronomen.scene: Kurz vor dem Unterricht — im Kursraum, Berlin

a1-42-welcher-dieser.lastLine: Dieser Weg hier ist schneller . Komm !
a1-42-welcher-dieser.intro: Vreni and Jonas hit a department store before the exam, debating which jacket looks best, which size fits, and which shop might actually have it in stock — every choice a "which one?" and a "this one": welche Jacke, diese Größe, dieses Geschäft.
a1-42-welcher-dieser.scene: Im Kaufhaus — vor der Prüfung, Berlin

a1-43-smalltalk-man.lastLine: Gute Idee ! Da kommt gerade unser Bus !
a1-43-smalltalk-man.intro: A rainy afternoon in the café. While they wait out the weather, the gang drifts into easy small talk — how’s it going, what’s the weekend look like, what’s Berlin like — and Yvonne keeps slipping in sentences with man to explain how things are done in Germany.
a1-43-smalltalk-man.scene: Im Café — ein verregneter Nachmittag, Berlin

a1-44-imperativ-modal2.intro: Marco wakes up sick the day before the exam, so he drags himself to Frau Dr. Berg. She examines him and fires off instructions — commands, what he may and may not do, and what he should take — while Marco, predictably, protests taking the medicine.
a1-44-imperativ-modal2.scene: Beim Arzt — einen Tag vor der Prüfung, Berlin

a1-45-telefonieren.intro: Still sick, Ben misses class and phones Solveig to get the homework. The line is bad, she talks too fast, and half the call is him asking her to repeat, spell and slow down — exactly the phrases you need on a real German phone call.
a1-45-telefonieren.scene: Ein Anruf — Ben ruft Solveig an, Berlin

a1-46-zeitangaben.lastLine: Perfekt ! Dann bleibe ich bis zum Schluss .
a1-46-zeitangaben.intro: Exam week is almost here. Wiebke lays out the schedule, and the group plans their last days — when they study, when they meet, when the test starts and what happens afterwards. Every plan hangs on a dative time phrase: am Freitag, seit Wochen, nach der Prüfung.

a1-47-goethe-final.intro: Exam day. Henrike and Timo wait nervously outside the Prüfungsraum, quizzing each other one last time. Then they go in — and a week later, both have news: Goethe A1 certificates. The end of the beginning.

a1-5-werbistdu.lastLine: vierundzwanzig . Und jetzt sind wir Partner !
a1-5-werbistdu.intro: A partner exercise. Two classmates, Lena and Paul, introduce themselves properly — names, where they are from, where they live, their age — and discover they are both new in Berlin.

a1-6-wfragen.intro: Break time turns into a two-person mini-interview. Sofia fires off the W-questions — where, when, why — and Felix answers, as two classmates turn small talk into real practice.

a1-7-jaodernein.intro: After class, Ben checks if Mia has time, then finds out how well they actually understand each other — quick-fire yes/no questions, honest answers, and one classic "say that again?" moment.

a1-8-goethemini1.lastLine: Zwei Sprachen . Der Test ist nicht schwer !
a1-8-goethemini1.intro: A quick partner checkpoint. Nina interviews Daniel using everything from Chapters 1–7 — name, age, origin — and discovers he comes from a country whose language surprises her.

a1-9-verben.intro: Phase 2 begins. Noah asks Clara what she does every day, and the two swap everyday routines — working, learning, cooking, playing — putting the new verb endings straight to work.

a2-1-genitiv.lastLine: Ja , gute Idee ! Ich rufe ihn sofort an .
a2-1-genitiv.intro: Season 2 begins. The Goethe A1 certificates have just been handed out, and the same classroom feels new: today is the first day of the A2 course. On the table lie books, bags, phones and photos — and the group discovers how naturally Germans say whose things they are: Annas Buch, Petras Handy, Rohan

a2-10-goethe-mini-1.lastLine: Ja , bestimmt ! Wir schaffen das zusammen !
a2-10-goethe-mini-1.intro: One week before the mock exam, the class runs a warm-up. Runa fires questions; she and Nick answer with everything they've built this phase — a Genitiv here, a weil-clause there, a modal in the Präteritum, a comparison with als. Nothing new is taught.
a2-10-goethe-mini-1.scene: Aufwärmen vor dem Goethe-Mini-Test — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-11-wenn.intro: It’s the last week before a long break — Wiebke is leaving for a sailing regatta in Argentina, and the class is planning a small farewell party. Every plan hangs on a condition: if the weather holds, if everyone’s free, whenever Wiebke checks his phone. That makes it the perfect stage for wenn, the
a2-11-wenn.scene: Abschiedsplanung vor den Ferien — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-12-reflexive-verben.intro: Enya’s sister is getting married on Saturday, and the whole class is caught up in the preparation — the dress, the cards, the nerves. Everyone is getting ready, hurrying, calming down, looking forward to it. Which makes it the perfect morning for reflexive verbs: sich beeilen, sich freuen, sich anzi
a2-12-reflexive-verben.scene: Der Morgen vor der Hochzeit — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-13-praepositionen-dativ.lastLine: rten Sie bitte . Ich gebe Ihnen eine Nummer .
a2-13-praepositionen-dativ.intro: Timo's bicycle has vanished somewhere between the bus stop and the museum, so the morning turns into a small city adventure: a trip to the police, a report filed with Frau Nissen, a coffee across from the station. Every step is a preposition of place and motion — mit dem Bus, zur Polizei, gegenüber
a2-13-praepositionen-dativ.scene: Ein Vormittag in der Stadt — Sprachschule Berlin
